DERATING: 100% of rated load from -40C to +60C ambient, then linear to 60% at +85C with a hard cutoff, natural convection. At 65C ambient that permits 92% against the 69-78% actually drawn, ~14 points of margin, and 78% stays legal to ~73.8C. Short-circuit protection is CONTINUOUS WITH AUTOMATIC RECOVERY, not latching

notes: The MPXV4006DP is ratiometric, so ITS SUPPLY IS ITS SCALE FACTOR - that is the whole reason for a separate reference here. description: Dual RRIO op-amp: breath buffer + reference buffer
notes: SOIC-8, and it RUNS ON +12V, NOT 5V: a +12V fault on the BREATH conductor is then at the rail, so there is no clamp current and the >=3.3k protection-resistor requirement goes away. Same part as the module op-amps - DEVICE FACTS ARE ON U-OPA-PITCH and are not repeated here. STABILITY IS THE WHOLE OF THIS ROW. The reference half drives the sensor's 100nF decoupler ALONE - C-REF-OUT is on the REF5050, not on this output (see figures.yaml cref-out-node). Against the specified 375 ohm open-loop Zo that is 1.5 degrees of phase margin as a bare follower, so IT MUST BE COMPENSATED, with TI's own dual-feedback network [SBOS737C Figure 56]: R-ISO-REF 37.4R, R-FB-REF 10k taken at VS, R-FBX-REF 100R + C-FB-REF 1nF at this pin. That gives 85.9 degrees AND exactly zero DC error across R-ISO-REF, so the 2% ratiometric objection to an out-of-loop resistor never has to be paid - see figures.yaml riso-ref-topology

description: Output and input capacitors on the REF5050
notes: REF5050 VIN bypass and REF5050 VOUT load capacitor - one each, with a 100nF from C-DECOUPLE-CARRIER alongside each. *** NEITHER IS ON THE BUFFER'S OUTPUT *** (see figures.yaml cref-out-node); this is the rail that IS the breath scale factor. The VOUT one is not a choice - the part cannot be built without it [SBOS410O 8.4.1 p.26: 'Confirm that a output capacitor (CL) is connected from VOUT to GND. For output stability, verify that the ESR value of CL less than or equal to 1.5 ohm', with Figure 8-6 giving CL = 1uF to 50uF] - and the other is the 8.4.1 supply bypass (1-10uF). That accounts for both and leaves nothing for the buffer output, which is just as well: 10uF there would be 10000x the OPA2197's 1 nF capacitive-load limit. CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING: the REF5050 now drives only the OPA2197's input bias current (+/-20 pA max at 25C), so its load regulation (20 ppm/mA typ, 30 max, 50 over temperature) contributes ZERO to the breath scale factor, where the other topology would have cost 300 ppm = 1.0 LSB. THE SERIES 1-1.5 OHM RESISTOR IS OPTIONAL, NOT REQUIRED - 8.4.1's 'ESR <= 1.5 ohm' is a stability CEILING an X7R satisfies trivially, and 9.4.1.1 p.29 says plainly 'A resistor in series with the output capacitor is optional.' FIT A 0R/1R0 FOOTPRINT and decide it at E13 with a scope; it is electrically free either way, being in series with a capacitor to ground rather than in the signal path. The TRIM/NR 1uF is DECLINED: 8.3.6 p.26 halves 4.5 uVrms to 2.25 uVrms and lengthens start-up, on a term already 325x below an ADC LSB (4.5 uVrms against 1.46 mV)

description: Isolation resistor, reference buffer dual-feedback network (SBOS737C Fig. 56)
notes: OPA2197 output to SKT-BREATH VS. One of four parts in TI's dual-feedback reference-buffer network [SBOS737C 8.2.3 p.30, Figure 56 'Precision Reference Buffer']; the other three are R-FB-REF, R-FBX-REF and C-FB-REF. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE. *** TI'S FIGURE TRANSFERS TO OUR 100 nF DESPITE ITS 10uF BECAUSE R_ISO IS SET BY Zo, NOT BY C_L *** - the attenuation R_ISO/(Zo+R_ISO) and the pole-zero ratio both depend only on R_ISO/Zo, and C_L moves both corners together and cancels. 37.4R is Zo/10 against the specified 375 ohm (see U-OPA-PITCH). Simulated 85.9 degrees at 896 kHz; the same model run on Figure 56 as printed returns 87.4 against TI's published 89. *** DC ERROR ACROSS THIS RESISTOR IS EXACTLY ZERO BY TOPOLOGY *** - C-FB-REF blocks at DC so no current flows in R-FBX-REF, input current is pA so none flows in R-FB-REF, and the amplifier therefore forces V(VS) = 5.000 V. Its value and tolerance stop mattering; the 1% is bought for stock reasons. Power is (10mA)^2 x 37.4 = 3.74 mW in an 0805. DO NOT PUT R_ISO INSIDE THE LOOP: it buys nothing at ANY value - 1.5 degrees at 10R and 1.5 degrees at 37.4R, the same as fitting nothing. See figures.yaml riso-ref-topology

description: DC feedback resistor, reference buffer - taken at the sensor's VS pin
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | 10k AND NOT TI'S 1M, deliberately. Two reasons TI's circuit does not have. (1) The guaranteed-over-temperature I_B of 5 nA through 1M is 5 mV = 1000 ppm = 3.4 LSB on a rail that IS the ratiometric scale factor; through 10k it is 50 uV = 0.034 LSB. (2) R_F x C_F sets the HANDOVER frequency above which the loop closes on the amplifier's own output instead of on VS. TI's load is a pure capacitor; ours draws 10 mA, so above the handover any load-current change appears at VS across R-ISO-REF. TI's 1M x 39nF puts it at 4.08 Hz, inside the breath channel. 10k x 1nF puts it at 15.9 kHz, well above the 500 Hz channel, and |Z_out| at VS is then 1.20 ohm at 500 Hz. The R-FB-REF:R-FBX-REF RATIO OF 100:1 IS WHAT MUST BE PRESERVED from TI, not the absolute values

description: AC feedback resistor, reference buffer - taken at the OPA2197 output pin
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | Scales with R-FB-REF to hold TI's 100:1 ratio, so that above the handover the loop closes on the amplifier output with only 1% of VS leaking in. R_Fx x C_F is 100 ns here against the 3.74 us TI's own rule (R_Fx C_F = R_ISO C_L) would give, and the simulation says it costs nothing - the binding condition is |R_Fx + 1/(2.pi.f C_F)| much less than R_F AT CROSSOVER, which at 896 kHz is 100 + 178 = 205 ohm against 10k, a 49x margin

description: AC feedback capacitor, reference buffer
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | C0G, because this capacitor sets the handover frequency and an X7R's DC-bias and temperature derating would move it. 1nF at R-FB-REF's 10k gives a 15.9 kHz handover. IT IS ALSO WHY THE DC ERROR IS ZERO: blocking at DC is what leaves R-FB-REF as the only feedback path, so the amplifier servos the SENSOR pin rather than its own output. NOTE FOR THE SPICE DECK: this network leaves the summing node with no DC path except through R-FB-REF, so a simulator needs a leak resistor there for convergence and a real board does not - the amplifier's input leakage provides it

description: Series resistor on each WS2815 data line at the driver
notes: TWO PARTS ON THE AGGRESSOR, against 63 on the victims. Standard practice at an addressable-LED driver: damps the fastest edge in the instrument at its source and protects the 74AHCT125 output. TWO, NOT FOUR - reverted 2026-09-21. This row went to four on the reasoning that the WS2815's BACKUP data line was connected to nothing and the level shifter's two spare gates were exactly what it needed. The datasheet (datasheets/led/WS2815.pdf) shows the vendor's own recommended circuit GROUNDING the first pixel's BI (L1 pin 6 to pin 5); from L2 onward BI comes from the PREVIOUS pixel's DI, internal to the tape, which is what makes the backup line lag by one and lets a dead pixel be bypassed. The head of the strip has nothing to lag. So BI is a ground connection, not a driven one: two gates, two resistors, and the LED loom stays at 6 conductors rather than 8. The figure is a raster with no text layer and was read by rendering at 700dpi - confirm visually before crimping

description: Series bead per supply branch
notes: One per branch: +12V analog, +12V umbilical, -12V, +5V. Chosen on ONE criterion - it is the only >=1A 600R 1206 part found whose datasheet publishes an IMPEDANCE-UNDER-DC-BIAS curve (traces at 0 / 250 / 500 / 1000 / 1500 mA). Off the drawing: Z@100MHz 600 nominal / 450 min / 750 max, DCR 0.080 ohm max, rated 1500 mA, 3.20 x 1.60 x 1.10 mm, -40 to +125degC including self-heating. *** A BEAD'S CURRENT RATING IS THERMAL, NOT MAGNETIC, so it says nothing about saturation *** - read the bias curve instead. At 100 MHz this part gives ~614 ohm at 0 A, ~431 at 250 mA, ~157 at 500 mA, ~72 at 1000 mA and ~51 at its RATED 1500 mA. Doubling the rating does not help: a 3000 mA twin in the same package reads ~145 ohm at 500 mA, slightly WORSE, for 0.02 ohm more DCR. PER BRANCH: FB4 (+5V, mA), FB3 (-12V, 10-20mA) and FB1 (+12V analog, ~45mA) all sit on the flat part and get 580-614 ohm, essentially the nameplate. *** FB2 CARRIES THE UMBILICAL AT figures.yaml umbilical-current AND GETS ROUGHLY HALF THAT *** - ~280-310 ohm, falling to ~245-275 ohm at the module total. EITHER restate FB2's requirement at its real operating current OR make FB2 a physically larger part. IR drop at 0.080 ohm max is 28.7 mV at the umbilical current (10.3 mW), 31.4 mV at the 392 mA module total, 3.6 mV at 45 mA. PINOUT: 1 ON, 2 FB, 3 PWRGD, 4 GND, 5 TIMER, 6 GATE, 7 SENSE, 8 VCC. *** FB, PIN 2, MUST BE DIVIDED DOWN FROM THE OUTPUT - NEVER LEFT OPEN. *** Foldback keys off V_FB, not off V_OUT ('the current folds back as a function of the output voltage, which is sensed at the FB pin', p.8), so with FB at 0V the limit sits at 12mV/50mohm = 240mA permanently, the output never charges, the timer ramps forever and the -1 latches. That is 'the instrument never starts', and no C-TIMER value fixes it; R-FB-HI/R-FB-LO are what set it. From the banked 164112fc.pdf: VCC UVLO 7.5 / 8.3 / 8.8 V, which holds GATE low regardless of ON; I_GATE -5 / -10 / -20 uA [p.2]; I_TIMER pull-up -24 / -80 / -132 uA [p.2]; the 12mV-to-47mV-at-VFB=0.5V law [Figure 7, p.9]. This row orders the CS8 (0 to +70degC); the IS8 is -40 to +85degC and is the better part for a rack that may sit in a hot van. notes: The FB divider. Its values and their derivation are the tracked figure loadswitch-fb-divider, owned by umbilical-load-switch.md and not restated here; what follows is what a reader of THIS row needs. FB must be divided down from the output at all - see U-LOADSW for why an open FB latches the part off. *** V_FB = 0.5V AND THE PWRGD THRESHOLD V_FBH = 1.313V ARE SET BY THE SAME DIVIDER, *** so V_OUT(full 47mV limit) = 0.381 x V_OUT(PWRGD) ALWAYS - 'cross 0.5V early in the ramp' and 'PWRGD means the output is good' are ONE decision, not two, and the ratio is fixed by the part, not by these resistors. It is therefore sized at the PWRGD end, which is the end with a hard requirement: PWRGD must release below the worst-case delivered output of ~11.36V (Eurorack +12V at -5%, less the sense and FET drops). The foldback law behind it, verbatim [p.5, drawn as Figure 7 p.9]: 'The current limit circuit will regulate the voltage across the sense resistor (VCC - VSENSE) to 47mV when VFB is 0.5V or higher. If VFB drops below 0.5V, the voltage across the sense resistor decreases linearly and stops at 12mV when VFB is 0V.' Divider current is 294uA at 12V, 294x the 1uA max FB input current [p.2], so leakage is <=0.34% of the ratio

description: Fault timer capacitor for U-LOADSW
notes: Fault timer capacitor for U-LOADSW. The value is the tracked figure loadswitch-timer and its derivation is in umbilical-load-switch.md; neither is restated here. TWO THINGS BIND WHEN BUYING IT. *** SPECIFY A LOW-LEAKAGE PART *** - at this value it is electrolytic or large ceramic, where leakage is a meaningful fraction of the 3 uA TIMER pull-down, and a leaky part means the timer never resets. And the package is through-hole radial or 1210 ceramic: an 0805 C0G cannot hold it. Fault time over the pull-up's own bounds is 587 / 160 / 95.6 ms, so the worst case is 95.6 ms against a 47.5 ms hot-plug start - 2.01x, which is the margin that actually had to be met. Datasheet hard minimum is 1.5 nF [p.5], not binding here

description: Gate capacitor programming the load switch ramp
notes: Programs the LT1641's output ramp: C = I_GATE / (dV/dt). The value and the ramp window it produces are the tracked figure loadswitch-gate-cap; do not restate them. THE THING TO KNOW BEFORE SIZING ANYTHING AROUND IT IS THAT I_GATE IS A 4:1 WINDOW - I_GATEUP = -5 / -10 / -20 uA [164112fc p.2], corroborated independently by the DC1354A demo quick-start guide p.1. *** SO ADR 0005's '50-100ms RAMP' IS NOT ACHIEVABLE WITH THIS PART: *** no single capacitor can hold a 4:1 current spread inside a 2:1 time window. The chosen value centres the TYPICAL inside ADR 0005 and the guaranteed envelope is wider. RAISED AGAINST ADR 0005 AND NOT DECIDED - either ADR 0005 widens the spec, or the ramp is programmed by something other than the internal pull-up. BOTH CORNERS ARE SAFE either way: 537mA of charging at the fast corner still clears the 240mA foldback floor at 0.14V of output and never approaches 940mA. C0G/NP0 or film, 50V - the dielectric matters, because a Y5V here re-programs the ramp with temperature. PACKAGE CORRECTED 2026-09-22: this row said '0805 or 1206'. C-FILT-MOD carries the same value in the same dielectric and its own notes say 82nF in C0G/NP0 almost certainly does not exist in 0805 - C0G permittivity puts that value in 1210 or larger. TWO ROWS, ONE VALUE, ONE DIELECTRIC, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM DOUBTED IT. Neither is verified against a capacitor datasheet - the bank holds none - so both now say 1210-or-film and both are open on the same question: confirm against a real part before ordering, or accept film

description: Panel power indicator
notes: A PLAIN POWER LED off the module's own rail, like every other Eurorack module's. It used to be driven by a presence comparator that watched the breath line - that comparator is DELETED, and with it the only thing in the module that tried to know whether the instrument was there. Health reporting belongs in the instrument, which has a display, a web app and the actual data. With LT1641-1 latching off on a fault, this still says why the instrument went dark

notes: ~4mA from the module's +12V analog rail. Was 820R from bus +5V when it shared a node with the level shifter's OE pins; that node is gone with the comparator

description: Hand-asserts the DAC8568 CLR during bring-up
notes: NORMALLY OPEN, AND IT IS COPPER - NOTHING IS ORDERED FOR THIS ROW, but the layout must carry the footprint. Two pads from CLR to AGND_MOD beside R-CLR-PU; shorting them pulls CLR low BY HAND, which is the only way to assert it - the watchdog that drove the net is not fitted and R-CLR-PU holds it inactive. E7-E10 pitch calibration wants a hand clear. Leave the DAC's clear-code register at its default so a manual assert parks every channel at zero scale

description: Pull-up holding the DAC8568 CLR inactive, with a bring-up pad
notes: THE WATCHDOG IS DELETED (U-WATCHDOG, R-WDT, C-WDT all gone), so CLR has no driver and is tied INACTIVE - pulled high. A solder pad to ground beside it lets CLR be asserted BY HAND, which E7-E10 want anyway: a 99ms watchdog would have fought every 'write a code, read the meter' step of pitch calibration. Leave the DAC's clear-code register at its default so a manual CLR still parks at zero scale. Do NOT write ClearIgnore

description: Straps the DAC8568 LDAC pin to GND
notes: *** LDAC MUST BE STRAPPED TO GND, NOT PULLED TO AVDD - PULLING IT HIGH GATES THE DAC. *** SBAS430E p.38, verbatim: 'For such synchronous updates, the LDAC pin is not required and it must be connected to GND permanently.' Same page: the internal LDAC register defaults to 0x00, and 'if the LDAC register bit is set to 0, the DAC channel is controlled by the LDAC pin'. So register at default plus pin high means the buffer-to-DAC-register transfer is BLOCKED - and with no MISO, firmware can never discover it. A module that accepts every word and moves no output. A hardware LDAC was considered and declined, so the six populated channels update as each word lands. WORTH REVISITING AT FIRMWARE TIME: SBAS430E Table 11 p.36 offers 'Write to DAC input register Ch X and update all DAC registers (SW LDAC)', so five plain writes then one update-all as the last word of each pass gives a SIMULTANEOUS update inside the six words already budgeted - taking the 100-200us CLR-exit window to zero for no parts and no ninth conductor

description: Octal 16-bit DAC SPI, internal reference
notes: *** THE ORDER CODE IS DAC8568ICPW, NOT DAC8568CIPW. *** DAC8568CIPW appears ZERO times in SBAS430E; the Package Option Addendum [pp.54-57] enumerates DAC8568IAPW / IBPW / ICPW / IDPW and the R reel variants. The I and the grade letter are transposed in several places including the banked file's own NAME, datasheets/analog/DAC8568CIPW.pdf - the file and its SHA are correct and renaming it would mean editing another wave's manifest fragment, which CLAUDE.md 4 forbids, so the fact is recorded here per repo-maintenance.md 3. GRADE LOCKED TO C, and the letter selects REFERENCE GAIN as well as reset state: A/B are gain 1 (2.500V full scale), C/D gain 2 (5.000V). An A-grade part would halve everything - pitch -2 to +2.25V, mods +/-5V - and channel 7 could not reach 2.500V at all. C also clears to ZERO scale where B/D clear to midscale and would park pitch octaves up: 'For device grades A and C on power-up, all DAC registers are filled with zeros and the output voltages of all DAC channels are set to zero scale.' *** THE C GRADE REQUIRES AVDD 5.0V TO 5.5V *** - C/D are specified only over that range where A/B are 2.7-5.5V. The LM317 nominal 5.21V passes, but E7 SELECTS R-REG-SET ON THE BENCH over a 0.66V worst-case spread, so 5.00V IS A HARD FLOOR ON THAT BENCH STEP. External VREFIN must be <= AVDD/2 on C/D against <= AVDD on A/B - not binding while the internal reference is used, but it forecloses an external-reference retrofit above ~2.6V. Reference tempco is GRADE-DEPENDENT: C/D 2 typ / 5 max ppm/degC against A/B 5 typ / 25 max, so the 5 ppm/degC in the pitch error budget is the C-grade MAX and is the right number. Populate 6 of 8: pitch, 4 mods, mod offset; channels 6 and 8 spare. Static reference mode auto-powers the reference with the DACs and Flexible mode (DB19=1) keeps it up regardless, but BOTH default to reference OFF after any power cycle - enable at boot

description: Level shifter, 3V3 SPI up to 5V for the DAC
notes: SAME part as the instrument LED shifter. Covers SCLK MOSI CS with a spare gate. Runs from bus +5V; the DAC runs from U-REG-DAC. *** NO INPUT CLAMP TO VCC, *** confirmed three independent ways in SCLS264O: abs-max lists 'Input clamp current, IIK (VI < 0): -20mA', NEGATIVE ONLY, against an output clamp specified BOTH ways; abs-max input voltage is -0.5 to 7V stated WITHOUT reference to VCC where the output is -0.5 to VCC+0.5; and input leakage is specified as +/-1uA max AT VI = 5.5V WITH VCC = 0V, which TI could not guarantee if a VCC clamp existed. THAT IS WHAT MAKES BACK-DRIVING AN UNPOWERED MODULE SAFE. V_IH 2.0V min and V_IL 0.8V max are TTL levels, NOT ratioed to VCC - the threshold the R-SPI-SER analysis is built on. Drive +/-8mA; input transition rate must be <= 20ns/V; TIE EVERY UNUSED INPUT TO VCC OR GND. *** OE IS TIED ENABLED AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. *** The presence-gated OE is deleted along with its comparator: the threshold sat inside the breath signal's own range, it locked out every standalone-module milestone, and it failed toward 'present'. What it was protecting against - floating CMOS at the DAC while the instrument is off - is what R-SPI-PULL's six resistors are for, and running the buffer unconditionally is what every surveyed Eurorack module does

description: Dual low-drift RRIO op-amp
notes: ONE op-amp part throughout the module, and THIS ROW IS WHERE THE OPA2197'S DEVICE FACTS LIVE - U-BUF and U-RESP cite it rather than repeat it. Six packages, twelve halves, TEN used: pitch, mod 1-4, mod offset follower, VREFOUT follower, breath REF-zero buffer, breath gain buffer, breath summer. TWO SPARE - and U-RESP claims both of them if it is fitted, so check that row before spending them. RRIO on +/-12V reaches ~11.9V. FROM THE BANKED SBOS737C: open-loop output impedance is SPECIFIED at 375 ohm [EC table p.8 and p.10, f = 1 MHz], with Figure 26 giving ~3.26k at 0.1Hz, 482 at 10Hz, a 375 plateau from 100Hz to 300kHz, 301 at 1MHz and ~73 at 10MHz - *** DO NOT SIZE A POLE OFF THE 10MHz VALUE, *** which is roughly 5x optimistic. Capacitive load is 1 nF max [p.1 Features, 7.3.5 p.22: 'in a unity-gain configuration, directly drives up to 1 nF of pure capacitive load'], and Figures 27/28 show that is a stable-but-RINGING limit, ~40% overshoot at unity gain - TI recommends a 10-20 ohm isolation resistor and tabulates R_ISO for 45/60 deg phase margin in Table 3 p.23. GBW 10MHz, SR 20V/us, Isc +/-65mA, IQ 1mA/amp, ~11.9V swing on +/-12V, SOIC-8 DUAL R-thJA 107.9 degC/W - note the SINGLE OPA197 is 115.8 and is a different table. PSRR is +/-1 uV/V typ and +/-3 uV/V max, i.e. 120 dB typ and 110.5 dB worst case; the '114 dB' figure is not in the document

part: 10k multiturn cermet + divider from the LM317 5.21V rail
description: Nulls the sensor's +0.265V pedestal at the INA828 REF pin
notes: Buffered by a half of U-OPA-PITCH - REF needs a low source impedance or it degrades CMRR one-for-one. *** RANGE 0 TO +1.0V, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE PEDESTAL IS A SPEC BAND, NOT A TYPICAL *** - the datasheet's own table gives Voff 0.152 / 0.265 / 0.378 V, so the REF needed spans 0.332-0.826V. A 0.6V ceiling would leave a part at the top of its own spec UN-NULLABLE, with 1.4-5.6% of span standing at the jack; +1.0V covers the whole band with margin. The setting itself is the tracked figure breath-zero-ref; do not restate it. *** DERIVE IT FROM THE LM317'S 5.21V RAIL, NOT FROM VREFOUT. *** VREFOUT is the DAC's internal reference and is DISABLED at power-on until firmware writes an enable, so taking the breath zero from it would make the analog breath path depend on a DAC register - which three documents correctly say it does not. The LM317 rail is up whenever +12V is. THIS IS ALSO WHAT MAKES THE PANEL KNOBS INDEPENDENT: with REF grounded the pedestal sits upstream of the gain pot and gets multiplied. One zero authority per representation still holds - this is CALIBRATION, set once, where the panel OFFSET knob is PERFORMANCE

description: Instrumentation amp - breath receiver, senses against AGND
notes: BREATH drives IN-, AGND drives IN+, and REF is driven by TRIM-BREATH-ZERO THROUGH A BUFFER - never a bare divider, because source impedance on an in-amp REF pin degrades CMRR one-for-one. *** THE NUMBER IS 5 OHMS *** [SBOS792A section 8.1, verbatim: 'For the best performance, keep the source impedance to the REF terminal, RREF, below 5 ohm'] - RREF sits in series with one of the internal 40k difference-amp resistors and unbalances the bridge. Output runs 0V at rest to inamp-full-scale: Vout = -2.16106*(V_BREATH - V_AGND) + V_REF, with TRIM-BREATH-ZERO nulling the sensor pedestal. *** NOTE THE GAIN: 2.16106 IS THE EFFECTIVE GAIN, *** the raw G = 1 + 50k/42.2k = 2.185 times the 1M/(1M+11k) bias divider - using the raw 2.185 is the recorded way to get this wrong. The DAC ch6 zero injection that originally justified the input swap is deleted (ADR 0003). EMI: the part HAS an integrated RFI filter, -3dB at 53MHz, and EMIRR is a TABULATED characteristic rather than just a curve. *** THE WORST CASES ARE 48dB DIFFERENTIAL AT 400MHz AND 51dB COMMON-MODE AT 1.8GHz, *** and the differential and common-mode columns INVERT between 900MHz (52/98) and 1.8GHz (94/51) - so any RF-rectification argument must use those two and not the 90-plus dB numbers. TI does not claim the internal filter is sufficient on its own. See breath-receive-stage.md

notes: Attenuator, NOT a feedback rheostat - a rheostat makes gain and offset share a resistor and the knobs fight, which is the coupling the REF trimmer removes one stage upstream. 0.125 to 1.000 against a fixed x4 = 0.5 to 4.0 at the jack. *** WIPER MUST BE BUFFERED: *** it drives R-IN, so an unbuffered wiper makes the gain depend on a source impedance that varies with rotation. (3) *** THE A/B LETTER IN RV09A / RV09B IS THE ROTATIONAL ANGLE *** (280 +/-5 deg vs 300 +/-5 deg), NOT THE TAPER; the taper is a separate A/B/C code, and this is a standing trap. (4) Body 9.8mm wide, 11.4mm across the snap-in lugs, 7.0mm board-to-shaft for every -40, shaft D6.0 0/-0.1 - three across 50.50mm is 34.2mm, so the pot body is nowhere near binding and the 14mm knob is the constraint. description: Nonlinear element for the response shaper
notes: Breath is unipolar so only one ever conducts in play; the second covers the power-on and fault excursions. Scaling is set at /2 so the knee lands at about a quarter of a hard blow - at /10 it would sit ABOVE the playing range and the control would do nothing until you overblow. *** THE 0.6 V KNEE THIS SHAPER DEPENDS ON IS NOT-IN-DOCUMENT AS A SPEC. *** Neither banked datasheet specifies V_F at 0.6V; it is readable only off Vishay's TYPICAL Fig.1 (~1mA at 25degC), and that curve shifts more than 100mV LEFT at 150degC - on a part whose entire behaviour is where the knee sits. Use Vishay's 440 K/W / 280mW as the conservative thermal pair; Diotec's 312 K/W / 400mW assume 3mm2 of copper per terminal. The plain 1N4148 is NEITHER package: it is leaded glass SOD27 (DO-35) axial. Which of the two SMD sizes to use is open and is decided by the board - either is electrically identical here

In series with R2 it is 0 to +2% of the ratio, and its ~100ppm/degC then contributes ~2ppm/degC - COMPARABLE to the LT5400 rather than 4-20x it, which was ADR 0006's own objection to its own trimmer. notes: MOVED. It now trims the reference the follower buffers, so it scales the intercept (k x V_ref) and touches the gain (1 + k) NOT AT ALL - a genuinely independent offset trim. R-OFFINJ is deleted with it: injecting into the inverting node was never a pure offset, because in a non-inverting stage that node sits at Vdac rather than at a virtual ground, so it added ~1% of gain and its span was one-sided. description: Compensation cap, op-amp OUTPUT to the inverting input
notes: FROM THE OP-AMP OUTPUT TO THE (-) INPUT. NOT 'across the feedback resistor' - with the tap at the jack, R2 spans jack-to-(-), so a cap across R2 connects the same two nodes and leaves R-OUT-PROT inside the loop at every frequency: 18 degrees of phase margin with 2m of cable, under 10 with four destinations. Three documents said 'across R2' and were wrong. 2.2nF with C-FILT-PITCH restored is maximally flat, -3dB at 12.2kHz. IT IS NOT A FILTER: a cap in the feedback of a NON-INVERTING stage gives (2+sRC)/(1+sRC), a pole and a zero an octave up, flattening at unity - 6.02dB maximum for any value. Two independent reviews found this separately

description: Anti-alias/glitch filter on the pitch DAC input, ahead of the op-amp
notes: THE ACTUAL PITCH FILTER. 15.9kHz against R-OPAMP-IN's 1k, on a node with NO LOOP AROUND IT. C-FB-PITCH cannot do this job: a cap across the feedback resistor of a NON-INVERTING stage gives (2+sRC)/(1+sRC) - a pole at 15.9kHz and a zero an octave above, flattening at unity, so 6.02dB of attenuation maximum for any value. It is a shelf, not a pole. Filtering the DAC before the stage is also what the surveyed designs do

part: Range-setting resistors for the two module trimmers
description: Sets TRIM-OFFSET's and TRIM-BREATH-ZERO's spans
notes: Both trimmers need a divider to set their span and neither had parts. TRIM-OFFSET wants ~+-50mV around 2.500V; TRIM-BREATH-ZERO wants 0 to +1.0V from the LM317 rail. Values with the stages at E10

description: Reconstruction and RF shunt at the pitch jack
notes: RESTORED. It was deleted on the reasoning that a cap on the feedback node sits inside the DC loop at the handover; two independent loop analyses then put 10nF there and found phase margin UNCHANGED, because C-FB-PITCH ties the (-) input to the op-amp OUTPUT so beta(inf)=1 and R-OUT-PROT isolates the jack above the handover. The feedback network is a LEAD at every load tried - open, 200pF, 800pF, 10nF, dead short. Deleting it cost 30dB at 1MHz and left the connector with no low-impedance shunt at all

description: DC bias path to ground at every DAC output pin
notes: AT THE DAC PIN, not after R-OPAMP-IN - 100k after the 1k would form a divider and cost 1% of gain. Without it the op-amp (+) inputs have no DC path to ground: their only connection is a DAC pin that may be high-Z before power-on reset, so outputs can sit at either rail during that window. The identical problem was already found and fixed on the breath in-amp (R-BIAS-INAMP); this is the same fix on the six DAC-driven nodes

description: Matched resistor network for pitch scaling
package: MSOP-8 MS8E (0.65mm pitch) WITH 1.88 x 1.68mm EXPOSED PAD
notes: RATIO IS 1:1 - the pitch stage is a non-inverting amp with the reference at the bottom of the feedback divider (see pitch-stage.md). Two of four sections used. ORDER CODE IS TWO LETTER FIELDS: LT5400 + <A|B matching> + <C|I|H|MP temp> + MS8E-1#PBF. The -1 option is the four-equal-10k 1:1 quad and THERE IS NO 1:3 OPTION [p.2 table: -1 10k 1:1, -2 100k 1:1, -3 1:10, -4 1k 1:1, -5 1M 1:1, -6 1:5]. Grade A is 0.01% matching, B 0.025%; A degrades to +/-0.0125% over -40/+85degC while B is flat. MUST BE THE MS8 (MSOP) OPTION, NOT THE LEADLESS DFN. *** MS8E HAS AN EXPOSED PAD *** [p.2, p.8] - the footprint is MSOP-8-1EP_3x3mm_P0.65mm_EP1.68x1.88mm, NOT a plain MSOP-8. WHERE THE PAD GOES [p.6]: not DC-connected to any resistor, 'do not tie the exposed pad to noisy signals or noisy grounds', 'connecting the exposed pad to a quiet AC ground is recommended'. OPEN, AND IT IS A LAYOUT DECISION NOBODY HAS MADE: pad-to-resistor coupling is 5.5 pF against 1.4 pF resistor-to-resistor, so THE PAD IS THE DOMINANT STRAY ON THE 1V/OCT NODE and nothing in this corpus says where it connects. Ratio tracking 1 ppm/degC MAX (0.2 typ). ABSOLUTE tolerance is +/-7.5% (A) / +/-15% (B), which sets TRIM-GAIN's real authority at 1.86-2.16% rather than a nominal 2%. WHY THE PART IS KEPT, since its own tempco is currently masked: the DAC's internal reference drifts 0.42 cents over 10degC and cannot be trimmed, against 0.027 for the LT5400 and 0.38 for two 0.1%/10ppm discretes - $8 permanently solves the one term that can be, on a board built once, and attacking the reference later is only worth doing if the network is already there. CAVEAT FOR ANYONE EDITING ADR 0006: the banked rev fa's option table ends at -6, so LT5400-7 and 'a 1:4 offered directly' are NOT-IN-DOCUMENT rather than refuted - do not 'correct' ADR 0006 by citing rev fa's silence. 5400fc.pdf is still wanted. *** STATUS MOVED selected -> open 2026-09-22: THE ORDER CODE IS INCOMPLETE. *** LT5400<A|B><C|I|H|MP>MS8E-1#PBF needs BOTH letters and neither is chosen anywhere in this corpus. DECIDED BY TWO THINGS, both cheap: matching grade A 0.01% against B 0.025% - and note A degrades to +/-0.0125% over -40/+85degC while B is flat, so A is not simply better - and the temperature grade, where C is 0 to +70degC in a rack that may sit in a hot van, the same argument already made for U-LOADSW's grade. A row marked 'selected' that cannot be put in a basket is the defect this status exists to prevent

description: Reconstruction filter cap on mod 1-4 outputs
notes: 1k x 82nF = 1.94kHz. Real attenuation on the 3.6kHz ZOH image that a 15.9kHz corner ignores. FOUR not five: breath does not pass through the DAC and has its own 330nF (C-OUT-BREATH, ~480Hz). ON THE JACK SIDE of R-OUT-PROT, never the op-amp side - inside the loop it is a capacitive load and the stage can oscillate. PACKAGE IS PROBABLY WRONG: 82nF in C0G/NP0 almost certainly does not exist in 0805 - C0G permittivity puts that value in 1210 or larger. Unverified because every distributor site was proxy-blocked. Options if it is not buyable: 1210, a film part, or raise the corner and take less attenuation on the 4kHz image

description: Feedback leg (R2) of each mod channel's two-resistor network
notes: R2 of each channel. R2/R1 = k = 3, so gain = 1+k = EXACTLY 4 and the intercept is k x V_ref with V_ref = 3.3333V from the offset channel - which lands the window on exactly +-10.000V. EIGHT RESISTORS FOR FOUR CHANNELS, not sixteen: do not order a four-resistor difference-amp set. Tolerance is worst case +-50.5mV of zero and -1.49/+1.52 percent of span, and same-sign parts cancel in the ratio, which is the reason for the one reel

description: Input leg (R1) of each mod channel's two-resistor network
notes: R1 of each channel, and it goes to the SHARED buffered reference from DAC ch7, NOT to ground - that is what makes a CLR park every jack at 0V. Four, one per channel. Order on one reel with R-MODGAIN-FB: reel-adjacent parts track and it is the RATIO that has to hold, not either absolute value

description: Eurorack front panel
notes: Laser or waterjet from DXF - SAME vendor and order as the key plate. 10HP (ADR 0004); this row said 8HP until 2026-09-22, which was the retired width. THE HEIGHT BUDGET IS THE TRACKED FIGURE panel-height-budget - do not restate it here, and note it was already over before POT-RESP was added

description: Series protection on each CV output
notes: *** SPECIFY 0.66-1W IN 1206 (ERJ-P08 class, confirmed to exist). THE POWER RATING IS NOT OPTIONAL AND THIS IS THE ONLY PART IN THE MODULE AT REAL RISK FROM ANY JACK FAULT. *** The worst case is output-to-output patching, not a short: with pitch taking jack-side feedback the loop FIGHTS the other module, giving 322mW against a 220R source at +/-10V (two reviewers found this independently, on 269/312/464mW ladders). A dead short merely rails the op-amp across this resistor, at 142mW. AND THE DERATING IS WHAT RULES OUT 500mW: thick-film at a 50C rack interior leaves a 500mW 1206 delivering 350-420mW, so it is ~1.1x margin, not the 2.6x a nameplate reading suggests. Mutable specifies its output 1k at >=200mW where every other resistor in the same BOM is 100mW, which is the published form of this argument

description: Series resistor on each op-amp + input driven by the DAC
notes: SEVEN. Now correct on the mod channels as well, because the two-resistor form drives the op-amp's (+) input directly - a true high-Z node where 1k causes no error. It was wrong on the OLD four-resistor version, where the 10k input resistor WAS the gain network and 1k in series unbalanced it. Pitch, mod 1-4, the mod offset buffer, the VREFOUT follower. DAC on 5.21V and op-amps on +-12V do not come up together; bounds clamp current, outside the feedback path so no accuracy cost

description: Clamp diodes on the DRIVER side of R-OUT-PROT
notes: MOVED to the op-amp side of the 1k, which fixes two things at once. (a) BACK-POWERING: clamped at the JACK, a neighbouring module driving 10V through its own 220R output pushes 42mA per jack into our +12V rail when this module is off - 254mA across six jacks, into the rail that also feeds the umbilical. Behind the 1k it is 7.6mA per jack. (b) LEAKAGE: inside the feedback loop the op-amp absorbs it, so the 2.4-cent BAT54S error goes to identically zero for any diode. BAV99 kept anyway - silicon costs nothing and the reasoning no longer depends on it. NOTE: no surveyed design clamps a CV output to the RAILS at all; every clamp in the corpus goes to GND. Erica Synths is the one that puts its clamp on the driver side, which is where this now is. SIX - one per OUTPUT jack including breath, whose schematic omitted it. The two BREATH INPUT clamps are a separate row, D-CLAMP-BREATH, so the module carries eight BAV99 in total

description: 3.5mm mono PCB-mount jack
notes: De facto eurorack standard. BUSHING IS D6.0mm WITH 4.5mm OF THREAD, so the panel hole is 6mm nominal and 6.2-6.5 in practice, with 5.5mm from the panel face to the body front including the shoulder. Body 9 x 9 x 8.3mm, barrel bore D3.6, 3.5mm of tails behind. Rated DC30V 0.5A, 5000 cycles, PBT / brass-Ni / BeCu-Ag. *** PINOUT, cross-checked two ways (drawing schematic, and a KiCad footprint whose pads are NAMED with offsets matching the drawing's 4.92 / 3.38 / 6.48): PIN 3 = TIP, PIN 2 = TIP-NORMAL SWITCH CONTACT - NORMALLY CLOSED TO PIN 3 AND OPENING WHEN A PLUG IS INSERTED - PIN 1 = SLEEVE. *** All three on one centreline, oval drill 1.6 x 0.6. LEAVE A 3mm HOLE OR A VOID IN THE PCB UNDER THE BARREL (Thonk's own note). THE SWITCH CONTACT IS FREE NORMALLING and nothing in the design uses it yet - worth knowing before the layout rather than after. FILED AT BOARD LEVEL, beside R-OUT-PROT, because three circuits drive these six jacks and panel.md owns only the cutouts: no single circuit page derives the connector

description: Keycap 16.5x16.5mm blank black MX stem

Compatible with: MX switches / Choc V1 switches'). Smaller than MX keycap spacing, which is the point. NOTE THE DOMAIN: taihao.com.tw is unreachable, www.tai-hao.com answers. notes: NOT ACETOXY. The common hardware-store type releases acetic acid while curing, inside a sealed cavity holding two dev boards, a carrier, connectors and a pressure sensor.
